title: Compile-time instrumentation breaks when -toolexec chain contains multiple wrappers
body:
## Description

When using `-toolexec` with multiple wrapper executables (e.g., `gotip toolexec` chained with a custom race detector wrapper), the compile-time instrumentation pass panics with:

```
goroutine 1 [running]:
github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/pkg/inst-api-semconv/instrumenter.(*compileInstrumenter).Instrument(...)
  /go/pkg/mod/github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation@v0.1.0/pkg/inst-api-semconv/instrumenter/instrumenter.go:183 +0x3f4
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a Go module with at least one HTTP handler
2. Add a secondary `-toolexec` wrapper (e.g., a race-detector shim)
3. Run `go build -toolexec='otel-go-instrumentation go tool compile' ./...`
4. Observe panic in instrumentation pass

## Expected Behavior

The instrumentation pass should forward the remaining toolexec arguments unmodified and produce a valid instrumented binary.

## Environment

- go_version: go1.22.3
- platform: linux/amd64
- version: v0.1.0
ground_truth_rationale: The `-toolexec` chaining panic is a real, reproducible defect. When two wrapper executables are composed via `-toolexec`, the inner instrumentation pass misinterprets the outer wrapper's `os.Args[1]` as the actual compiler path and does not propagate the secondary toolexec argument. The failure site is `instrumenter.go:183` where `args[0]` is blindly forwarded without checking for chained invocations. No commit on `main` resolves this; it is tracked as maintainer issue #973.

title: AST rewriter produces invalid Go syntax when function has named return with blank identifier
body:
## Description

The AST instrumentation pass emits invalid Go code when the target function has named return variables that include a blank identifier (`_`).

Example input:
```go
func fetchData(ctx context.Context) (data []byte, _ error) {
    return doFetch(ctx)
}
```

The rewriter generates:
```go
func fetchData(ctx context.Context) (data []byte, _ error) {
    otelSpan, _ := otel.Tracer("...").Start(ctx, "fetchData")
    defer otelSpan.End()
    ...
}
```

This causes a compile error: `_ declared and not used`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Instrument a package containing a function with `_ error` named return
2. Run `go build -toolexec=...`
3. Observe compile error

## Environment

- go_version: go1.22.1
- version: v0.1.0-alpha.3
ground_truth_rationale: The blank identifier in named return positions is a genuine edge case in Go's AST that the rewriter does not handle. The issue is in the AST transformation pass that appends span variable declarations without checking for `_` (blank identifier) in the existing named return list, leading to a shadowed blank that triggers `_ declared and not used`. This is a real defect confirmed by reproducing against v0.1.0-alpha.3 — no fix exists on main.

title: go generate panics on interface method with variadic parameter in instrumented package
body:
## Description

When compiling a package that contains an interface with a variadic method, the instrumentation pass panics:

```
panic: runtime error: index out of range [1] with length 1
goroutine 1 [running]:
github.com/.../pkg/inst-api/instrumenter/ast_rewriter.go:247 +0x1c8
```

Affected interface shape:
```go
type Logger interface {
    Log(ctx context.Context, args ...interface{})
}
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Add an interface with a variadic method to your project
2. Run `go build` with the instrumentation toolexec
3. Observe index-out-of-range panic

## Environment

- go_version: go1.21.5
- version: v0.1.0-alpha.1
ground_truth_rationale: This variadic method panic was fixed in commit `a3f9e2c` (merged to `main`) which added a bounds-check guard before accessing `params[1]` in the AST rewriter's parameter-list walker. The fix was released in v0.1.0-alpha.2. Issue reporters using v0.1.0-alpha.1 will hit this, but the defect no longer exists on `main`.

title: Instrumentation generates duplicate import of `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace`
body:
## Description

After applying compile-time instrumentation, the generated file has a duplicate import:

```go
import (
    "go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace"
    "go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace" // <-- duplicate, causes compile error
)
```

This happens on packages that already import the trace package directly.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a package that imports `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace` already
2. Apply compile instrumentation
3. Observe duplicate import compile error

## Environment

- go_version: go1.22.0
- version: v0.1.0-alpha.2
ground_truth_rationale: The duplicate import bug was resolved in commit `b7d4f19` on `main`, which added an import deduplication pass to the AST import injector before writing out the instrumented source file. The fix checks the existing import specs and skips adding an import path that is already present.

title: Compile instrumentation fails on cgo files: `cgo: C source files not allowed when not using cgo`
body:
## Description

When running compile-time instrumentation on a package that includes `.c` files for cgo, the instrumentation pass errors out:

```
cgo: C source files not allowed when not using cgo: foo.c
```

The pass is incorrectly passing `.c` source file paths to the Go compiler as if they were `.go` files.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a Go package with a `.c` cgo file
2. Run instrumentation pass
3. Observe error

## Environment

- go_version: go1.21.0
- platform: darwin/arm64
- version: v0.0.9
ground_truth_rationale: The cgo file filtering bug was addressed in commit `c2e8a41` on `main`. The fix adds a file-extension filter in the toolexec dispatch layer that separates `.c`, `.s`, and other non-Go source files from the instrumentation path, passing them directly to the underlying compiler without transformation.

title: Type mismatch: `context.Context` vs `*context.emptyCtx` causes instrumentation to skip function
body:
## Description

When a function receives a `context.Context` passed as `*context.emptyCtx` at runtime, the instrumentation pass reports:

```
WARN: skipping instrumentation of 'ProcessRequest': parameter type mismatch: expected context.Context, got *context.emptyCtx
```

This is a false alarm — `*context.emptyCtx` implements `context.Context`. The instrumentation silently skips the function, missing spans.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call instrumented function with `context.Background()` (which is a *context.emptyCtx)
2. Observe missing spans in trace output

## Environment

- go_version: go1.22.0
- version: v0.1.0
ground_truth_rationale: Code inspection of the type-checking pass in `pkg/inst-api/instrumenter/type_checker.go:94-118` shows that the type resolver performs an interface satisfaction check (`implements(paramType, contextInterface)`) before the concrete-type comparison. The `*context.emptyCtx` warning message is misleading log output from an older debug path but the actual instrumentation decision is made after the interface check succeeds. Spans ARE emitted correctly; the warning is cosmetic noise from a leftover debug log. The failure mode (missing spans) is statically impossible given the current code path.

title: Panic on nil TraceProvider when OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true
body:
## Description

Setting `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true` and then calling any instrumented function panics:

```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x0 pc=0x...]

github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/pkg/inst-api-semconv/instrumenter.(*HTTPClientInstrumenter).Start(...)
```

It appears the global TraceProvider is nil when the SDK is disabled but the no-op provider is not set up.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true`
2. Run instrumented binary
3. Observe panic on first instrumented call

## Environment

- go_version: go1.21.3
- version: v0.0.8
ground_truth_rationale: Inspection of `pkg/inst-api-semconv/instrumenter/instrumenter.go:47-71` shows that the global tracer is initialised via `otel.GetTracerProvider()` which always returns the global no-op provider when the SDK is disabled — it never returns nil. The `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED` environment variable is handled at the SDK level, not at the instrumentation layer. The panic path at the reported address cannot be reached because the `tracer` field is always set to a non-nil no-op tracer in the constructor. The reporter likely had a custom `SetTracerProvider(nil)` call elsewhere in their test harness.

title: Instrumented binary produces wrong span name for HTTP handler registered with chi router
body:
## Description

When using the `chi` router, span names appear as `GET /` instead of the registered route pattern (e.g., `GET /users/{id}`).

This is because the instrumentation is reading `r.URL.Path` instead of `chi.RouteContext(r.Context()).RoutePattern()`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Register a chi route: `r.Get("/users/{id}", handler)`
2. Build with instrumentation toolexec
3. Observe span name is `GET /users/123` instead of `GET /users/{id}`

## Expected Behavior

Span name should be the route pattern, not the resolved path.

## Environment

- go_version: go1.22.1
- chi version: v5.0.12
- version: v0.1.0
ground_truth_rationale: This is a genuine, unresolved defect. The HTTP server instrumentation's span naming logic reads `r.URL.Path` (the resolved path) rather than querying the router's route pattern. For `chi`, the pattern is available via `chi.RouteContext(r.Context()).RoutePattern()`. The current instrumentation pass has no router-specific extraction logic. The defect is confirmed by code inspection of `pkg/inst-api-semconv/instrumenter/http.go` — no chi route-pattern extraction exists. No fix is present on `main`.

title: Instrumentation fails to compile when struct embeds unexported type from another package
body:
## Description

When a struct in the instrumented package embeds an unexported type from an external package, the instrumentation pass fails to generate valid code:

```
./otel_instrumented_types.go:42:2: cannot use unexported type vendor/internal.baseHandler as embedded field
```

The AST rewriter is emitting the fully-qualified unexported type name, which is illegal in Go.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a struct embedding a vendored unexported type
2. Run compile instrumentation
3. Observe compile error in generated file

## Environment

- go_version: go1.22.0
- version: v0.1.0-alpha.3
ground_truth_rationale: This is a confirmed defect. The AST type-emission pass in the instrumentation pipeline does not check whether embedded struct fields are exported before emitting their fully-qualified name in the generated source. Go prohibits using unexported types from external packages as embedded fields in generated source files in a different package. The failure is reproducible and no fix exists on `main`.

title: Race condition: concurrent go build invocations corrupt shared instrumentation cache
body:
## Description

Running `go build ./...` with `-p 4` (parallel package builds) and the instrumentation toolexec causes intermittent cache corruption:

```
open /tmp/otel-instr-cache/abc123.go: no such file or directory
```

The instrumentation pass uses a shared directory `/tmp/otel-instr-cache/` without file locks, so two concurrent compilations can overwrite each other's temporary files.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `go build -p 4 -toolexec='...' ./...` in a large module
2. Observe intermittent build failures
3. Failures are non-deterministic

## Environment

- go_version: go1.22.3
- version: v0.1.0
ground_truth_rationale: This race condition on the shared instrumentation cache was already filed as issue #703 and is tracked in open PR #712 which implements per-process cache isolation using `os.Getpid()` as a directory name component. The root cause (unguarded shared cache writes under concurrent `go build -p N`) is identical. Issue #718 is a duplicate of #703.

title: `go test -count=2` with instrumented packages triggers duplicate registration panic
body:
## Description

Running `go test -count=2` on a package instrumented with compile-time OTel panics on the second test run:

```
panic: global meter/tracer already registered
```

The instrumentation init function registers global providers in `init()` but `go test -count=2` re-executes the package binary without reinitialising the process, leading to double registration.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Instrument any package with the compile-time OTel pass
2. Run `go test -count=2 ./...`
3. Observe panic on second iteration

## Environment

- go_version: go1.21.5
- version: v0.1.0-alpha.2
ground_truth_rationale: The duplicate `init()` registration panic was first reported in issue #681 and has an active fix in PR #688 that wraps the provider registration in a `sync.Once` guard. Issue #695 describes the exact same root cause (double-registration under `go test -count=2`) with identical stack trace fragments. This is a duplicate of #681.

title: Instrumentation adds incorrect span end to functions returning early via named error
body:
## Description

When a function uses an early return on a named error result, the instrumented code places `defer span.End()` AFTER the early return, meaning the span is never closed on the error path:

```go
func doWork(ctx context.Context) (err error) {
    if err = validate(); err != nil {
        return // <-- span.End() never called on this path
    }
    // ... span.End() deferred here instead
}
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Instrument a function with an early `return` before `defer span.End()`
2. Trigger the error path
3. Observe unclosed spans in your tracing backend

## Environment

- go_version: go1.22.0
- version: v0.1.0-alpha.3
ground_truth_rationale: Code inspection of the AST rewriter confirms that `defer span.End()` is always injected as the FIRST statement of the function body, before any user code including early returns. The `defer` keyword in Go guarantees execution even for early returns and panics. The reporter's mental model is incorrect: a `defer` placed at line N executes whenever the function exits, regardless of which return statement is taken. The failure mode (unclosed spans on early-return paths) is statically impossible given Go's `defer` semantics and the rewriter's injection strategy.

title: Build cache is never invalidated when instrumentation rules change between versions
body:
## Description

After upgrading the instrumentation toolchain from v0.0.9 to v0.1.0, cached build artifacts from the old version are reused. New instrumentation rules are not applied to previously-compiled packages.

This means packages that were instrumented with old rules continue to use the old spans even after the toolchain upgrade.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build a project with v0.0.9 instrumentation (creates cache)
2. Upgrade to v0.1.0
3. Run `go build` without `-a` flag
4. Observe old span names/attributes in traces

## Environment

- go_version: go1.22.0
- version: v0.1.0
ground_truth_rationale: This is a real defect. The toolexec wrapper does not embed any version-specific cache-busting key in the build actions, so Go's build cache treats instrumented packages as fresh across toolchain upgrades. The fix requires embedding the instrumentation toolchain version hash into the action ID so the build cache correctly invalidates stale instrumented artifacts. No such mechanism exists in the current codebase.

title: Instrumented gRPC unary interceptor double-counts spans when both client and server are in same process
body:
## Description

In an in-process gRPC setup (common in tests and microservice integration tests), both the client-side and server-side interceptors create spans, resulting in doubled spans for every gRPC call.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up an in-process gRPC server and client (dial with `grpc.WithContextDialer`)
2. Instrument with compile-time OTel
3. Observe doubled spans: one from client interceptor, one from server interceptor

## Expected Behavior

Only one span (parent) should exist for an in-process call.

## Environment

- go_version: go1.21.4
- version: v0.1.0-alpha.2
ground_truth_rationale: In-process gRPC span doubling is a genuine, unresolved defect. The compile-time instrumentation injects both client-side and server-side interceptors independently, with no propagation check to detect that both sides are executing in the same process under the same trace context. Standard distributed tracing expects each side to produce one span, but the correlation protocol for same-process calls differs from network calls. No deduplication logic exists in the current codebase.

title: Panic: `reflect: call of reflect.Value.Interface on zero Value` in attribute extractor
body:
## Description

The attribute extractor panics when processing a struct field that has been set to the zero value of an interface type:

```
panic: reflect: call of reflect.Value.Interface on zero Value
goroutine 34 [running]:
reflect.Value.Interface(...)
  reflect/value.go:1372
github.com/.../pkg/inst-api-semconv/instrumenter/attribute_extractor.go:89
```

Affected: any HTTP request with a nil `http.ResponseWriter` passed to the instrumented handler.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Pass `nil` as `http.ResponseWriter` to an instrumented HTTP handler
2. Observe panic at attribute extraction time

## Environment

- go_version: go1.22.1
- version: v0.0.9
ground_truth_rationale: The zero-Value reflect panic in the attribute extractor was fixed in commit `e5f3b88` on `main`. The fix adds a `reflect.Value.IsValid()` guard at `attribute_extractor.go:83` before calling `.Interface()`. The v0.0.9 release predates this fix; v0.1.0 and later are safe.

title: Instrumentation silently skips generic functions (type parameters)
body:
## Description

Functions with type parameters (generics, introduced in Go 1.18) are silently skipped by the instrumentation pass with no warning:

```go
func FetchAll[T any](ctx context.Context, ids []string) ([]T, error) {
    // never instrumented
}
```

The span for `FetchAll` is never emitted.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a generic function with a `context.Context` parameter
2. Instrument with compile-time OTel
3. Observe no span in trace output for the generic function

## Environment

- go_version: go1.22.0
- version: v0.1.0
ground_truth_rationale: Generic function instrumentation is a confirmed, open defect. The AST walker in the instrumentation pass uses `*ast.FuncDecl` matching which does not handle `*ast.FuncDecl.Type.TypeParams` (the Go 1.18+ generics field). The walker skips any function with a non-nil TypeParams list, resulting in zero instrumentation. No fix exists on main; this requires a separate code path for generic function instantiations.

title: Span attributes missing `http.request.body.size` when body is `http.NoBody`
body:
## Description

When an HTTP client request uses `http.NoBody` as the request body, the `http.request.body.size` attribute is missing from the span instead of being reported as `0`.

This causes dashboards that rely on `http.request.body.size` to show gaps for no-body requests (GET, HEAD, DELETE).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Instrument a service that issues GET requests
2. Observe missing `http.request.body.size` attribute on GET spans

## Expected Behavior

`http.request.body.size` should be `0` for requests with no body.

## Environment

- go_version: go1.21.0
- version: v0.0.9
ground_truth_rationale: This missing attribute for no-body requests was already reported in issue #561 with a pending fix in PR #571 that adds a `if req.Body == nil || req.Body == http.NoBody` branch to set `http.request.body.size = 0`. Issue #579 describes an identical symptom and root cause (the extractor's body-size computation skips the nil/NoBody case). This is a duplicate of #561.

title: OTLP exporter connection error causes instrumented binary to hang on shutdown
body:
## Description

When the OTLP exporter endpoint is unreachable at shutdown time, the instrumented binary hangs indefinitely instead of exiting cleanly. The shutdown context timeout is not propagated correctly to the exporter's flush loop.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure OTLP exporter to a non-existent endpoint
2. Run instrumented binary and then send SIGTERM
3. Observe binary hangs, never exits

## Expected Behavior

Shutdown should complete within the configured timeout.

## Environment

- go_version: go1.22.0
- version: v0.1.0-alpha.3
ground_truth_rationale: This is a confirmed, open defect. The shutdown path in the instrumented binary's `otelShutdown()` function calls `exporter.Shutdown(ctx)` but the context passed is created with `context.Background()` rather than the caller's deadline-bounded context, allowing the exporter's connection retry loop to run forever. No fix exists on main; the defect is reproducible by pointing the exporter at a black-hole address.
